about: Every OAuth app and MCP client approval Spade needs from a maker. The source for spade/docs/connector-registrations.md; bun run docs:connectors --check compares it with apps/cloud/src/broker/apps.ts and spade/config/connector-apps.json. Never a client secret.

app.name: Spade
app.description: Spade is the assistant in ace. It connects to your apps through their MCP servers, on your own computer.

registrations.name: Google Workspace (Gmail, Calendar, Chat, Docs, Drive, Sheets, Slides)
registrations.blocked_on: Owner parked it: OAuth verification plus the yearly security assessment for the restricted scopes
registrations.where: Google Cloud console > Google Auth Platform > Clients > Create Client, type Web application, in one project for all seven apps.
notes: First turn on the Gmail, Calendar, Chat, Docs, Drive, Sheets and Slides APIs and their MCP APIs in the project (https://developers.google.com/workspace/guides/configure-mcp-servers).
The consent screen (Branding, Audience, Data Access) is External and in production.
Google's OAuth verification is needed for the sensitive scopes, and Gmail and Drive's restricted scopes also need its yearly security assessment.
One client and one pair of secrets serve all seven apps.

registrations.name: Figma
registrations.blocked_on: Figma paused new MCP clients; the access request is on file for when they resume
registrations.ask: We build Spade, the assistant in ace, an open-source MCP client that runs on people's own computers. We'd like Spade listed in Figma's MCP catalog so our users can connect Figma's remote MCP server. Spade identifies itself with a client ID metadata document and signs in through a loopback redirect.
notes: Figma: "only clients listed in the catalog can connect" (https://developers.figma.com/docs/figma-mcp-server/remote-server-installation/).
Once Figma says yes, remove "waits_for": "maker_approval" from Figma's entry in spade/config/connectors.json and release.

registrations.name: Vercel
registrations.ask: We build Spade, the assistant in ace, an open-source MCP client that runs on people's own computers. We'd like Vercel to review Spade as an MCP client so our users can connect Vercel MCP. Spade identifies itself with a client ID metadata document and signs in through a loopback redirect.

form.answer: {redirect} (loopback: Spade listens on a free port on 127.0.0.1, as RFC 8252 allows)

Install ace from https://acehq.dev/download and open it. In Spade, go to Settings > Spade > Connectors > Connect an app, choose Vercel and sign in with your Vercel account. Then open a project: ask Spade to show one of your Vercel projects and its latest deployment.
Spade is open source under Apache-2.0. It identifies itself with the client ID metadata document {client_document}, which Vercel's authorization server can fetch.

notes: The form is linked from https://vercel.com/docs/agent-resources/vercel-mcp.
No review is needed once Vercel's metadata says authorization_response_iss_parameter_supported: Spade's client ID metadata document then works as it is.
Once Vercel says yes, remove "waits_for": "maker_approval" from Vercel's entry in spade/config/connectors.json and release.

registrations.name: Pipedrive
registrations.blocked_on: Posting on Pipedrive's developer community needs the owner's signed-in account
registrations.ask: We build Spade, the assistant in ace, an open-source MCP client that runs on people's own computers. We'd like Pipedrive to approve Spade's client ID metadata document and its loopback redirect, on any port, so our users can connect Pipedrive's MCP server.
registrations.channel: A post on Pipedrive's developer community
notes: Once Pipedrive says yes, remove "waits_for": "maker_approval" from Pipedrive's entry in spade/config/connectors.json and release.

registrations.name: Ramp
registrations.ask: We build Spade, the assistant in ace, an open-source MCP client that runs on people's own computers. We'd like Ramp to allowlist Spade's redirect URI so our users can connect Ramp MCP. Spade identifies itself with a client ID metadata document.
notes: Ramp: "custom clients and gateways must have their exact redirect URI allowlisted" (https://support.ramp.com/ramp-mcp/).
Once Ramp says yes, remove "waits_for": "maker_approval" from Ramp's entry in spade/config/connectors.json and release.

registrations.name: Canva
registrations.where: Canva Developer Portal > Your apps > Create an app > Outside Canva, then Configuration > Integration methods > Canva MCP on.
notes: Public integrations are reviewed by Canva; private ones are only for Enterprise teams (https://www.canva.dev/docs/connect/creating-integrations/).

registrations.name: Slack
registrations.where: Slack API > Your Apps > Create New App > From a manifest, or bun run docs:connectors slack --yes.
notes: Scopes are user scopes, not bot scopes.

Slack: "only directory-published apps or internal apps may use MCP" (https://docs.slack.dev/ai/slack-mcp-server/). Until Spade is listed in the Slack Marketplace it works only in the owner's own workspace.

registrations.name: Box
registrations.where: Box Admin Console > Integrations > Box MCP server > Configure > Additional Configuration > Add Integration Credentials (Box's guide doesn't give the console's address).
notes: No scopes to enter: Box sets its own, and the broker asks for none.
Credentials are made per enterprise by a Box admin. Box may limit them to the owner's enterprise; its docs don't say they work in other enterprises, so one shipped client may not be possible.

registrations.name: Zoom
registrations.where: Zoom App Marketplace > Develop > Build app > General app (user-managed OAuth) > Create.
notes: People outside the owner's Zoom account can sign in only once the app is published to the Zoom App Marketplace (https://developers.zoom.us/docs/mcp/servers/connect-to-zoom-mcp-servers/).

registrations.name: GitHub
registrations.where: GitHub > Settings > Developer settings > OAuth Apps > New OAuth App, signed in as the account or organisation that should own it.
notes: Check Enable Device Flow. GitHub requires a callback URL; the device flow doesn't use it.
Don't generate a client secret: Spade never uses one, and the repository refuses one.
Copy the Client ID into spade/config/connector-apps.json as the client_id of the github entry and commit it; it is public by design.
If the owner is an organisation that restricts OAuth apps, approve Spade under its third-party access settings.

registrations.name: Asana
registrations.where: Asana developer console > Create new app > MCP app, then OAuth and Manage distribution in the sidebar.
notes: Asana's V2 MCP server has no dynamic registration: every client registers first (https://developers.asana.com/docs/integrating-with-asanas-mcp-server).

registrations.name: HubSpot
registrations.where: HubSpot > Development > MCP Connectors > Create MCP connector.
notes: No scopes to enter: HubSpot sets its own, and the broker asks for none.

registrations.name: Front
registrations.where: Front > Settings > Company > Developer: create the app, then Features > Add feature > Front MCP, with OAuth on.
notes: Front may require publishing the app before people at other companies can sign in (https://dev.frontapp.com/docs/mcp-server).
